Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And he made the altar of burnt-offering from acacia wood: five cubits its length, and five cubits its width, square, and three cubits its height.
translations.2: And he made its horns upon its four sides — its horns were from it — and he overlaid it with copper.
translations.3: And he made all its vessels: the pots, and the shovels, and the basins, and the forks, and the fire-pans; all of these he made of copper.
translations.4: And he made for it a grating, fashioned after the manner of netting, of copper, below its ledge, from the bottom up to its midpoint.
translations.5: And he cast four rings upon the four sides of the copper grating, as a place for the poles.
translations.6: And he made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with copper.
translations.7: And he inserted the poles into the rings upon the two sides of the altar, to carry it by them — hollow planks he made it.
translations.8: And he made the laver and its base of copper, from the mirrors of the women who assembled at the entrance of the tent of the assembly.
translations.9: And he made the enclosure on the side toward the direction of the south wind — the curtains of the enclosure of fine twisted linen, one hundred cubits.
translations.10: Its pillars were twenty, and their bases twenty of copper; and the clasps of the pillars and their overlay were silver.
translations.11: And on the side of the north, one hundred cubits; its pillars were twenty, and their bases twenty of copper; and the clasps of the pillars and their overlay were silver.
translations.12: And on the side toward the direction of the west wind, curtains of fifty cubits in length; their pillars were ten, and their bases ten; and the clasps of the pillars and their overlay were silver.
translations.13: And on the side toward the direction of the east, fifty cubits.
translations.14: Of these, curtains of fifteen cubits for the one shoulder; their pillars were three, and their bases three.
translations.15: And for the second shoulder, right and left of the entrance of the enclosure, curtains of fifteen cubits in length; their pillars were three, and their bases three.
translations.16: All the curtains of the enclosure, all around, were of fine twisted linen.
translations.17: And the bases of the pillars were of copper; and the clasps of the pillars and their overlay were silver; and he overlaid their tops as well — for all of them were overlaid with silver.
translations.18: And the screen of the entrance of the enclosure was the work of an embroiderer, of blue and purple and scarlet dye and fine twisted linen; and its length was twenty cubits, and its thickness — which is its width — five cubits, corresponding to the curtains of the enclosure.
translations.19: And its pillars were four, and their bases four of copper; and their clasps were silver; and he overlaid their tops and their overlay was silver.
translations.20: And all the pegs of the tabernacle and of the enclosure, all around, were of copper.
translations.21: This is the count of what went into the tabernacle — the tabernacle of the testimony — which was reckoned by the command of Moses, as the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
translations.22: That which Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made — according to all that God had commanded Moses.
translations.23: And with him Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan — a master and skilled craftsman, and an embroiderer in blue and purple and scarlet dye and linen.
translations.24: Now the gold that was used in the work, for all the work of the sanctuary — the total of the gold of the wave-offering was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
translations.25: And the silver — the total of what was obtained from the counted ones of the congregation was one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
translations.26: A half-shekel for each head, half a shekel by the shekel of the sanctuary, for every one who passed through the counting, from twenty years of age and upward — for six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty.
translations.27: And from the hundred talents of silver were cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil — one hundred bases from one hundred talents, one base from one talent.
translations.28: And the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels — from them he made clasps for the pillars, and overlaid their tops and overlaid them.
translations.29: And the copper of the wave-offering amounted to seventy talents and two thousand and four hundred shekels.
translations.30: And from it he made the bases of the entrance of the tent of the assembly, and the copper altar, and the copper grating that belongs to it, and all the vessels of the altar.
translations.31: And the bases of the enclosure all around, and the bases of its entrance, and all the pegs of the tabernacle, and all the pegs of the enclosure all around.
